title: Exponential Quantum Speed-Up for DDT Attacks
summary: A quadratic quantum speed-up is known for a DDT-supported differential distinguisher, but an exponential advantage despite efficient classical DDT sampling remains open.

formal_statement.body: For a function $F$, its DDT can be sampled efficiently by choosing random plaintexts $x_1$ and $x_2$ and obtaining $(\Delta_I,\Delta_O)=(x_1\oplus x_2,F(x_1)\oplus F(x_2))$. This efficient classical sampling is a fundamental obstacle to transferring Simon's exponential quantum speed-up, which does not automatically apply to DDT-based attacks. Determine whether a DDT-based cryptanalytic attack can nevertheless achieve an exponential quantum speed-up over its corresponding classical attack and, if so, how it overcomes this sampling barrier.

scope.domain: Quantum differential cryptanalysis of difference-distribution-table-based attacks.
parameters: F: function whose DDT is sampled
x₁ and x₂: random plaintexts used to obtain a classical DDT sample
ΔI and ΔO: input and output differences in the sample
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a DDT-based cryptanalytic attack can achieve an exponential quantum speed-up over its corresponding classical attack and how it could overcome efficient classical DDT sampling.

citations.label: A Geometric Approach to Quantum Distinguishers

progress.summary: The source reports a quadratic speed-up for a DDT-supported differential distinguisher, then explicitly asks whether an exponential speed-up is possible. It identifies efficient classical DDT sampling as the barrier and excludes only a direct Simon/Bernstein–Vazirani-style route, not every DDT-based attack.
citation_labels: Zhili Wu et al., A Geometric Approach to Quantum Distinguishers
